scope: generic research library; movement claims link master

sources.title: OpenSim: Simulating musculoskeletal dynamics and neuromuscular control to study human and animal movement
supports: Extensible musculoskeletal dynamics, muscle analysis, simulation and controller components.
APIs expose moment arms, fiber lengths and passive forces.
limitations: Software capabilities do not validate an assembled patient model or neural injury mechanism.
Paper describes historical software; exact offline version remains to be selected.

license.value: Article CC BY; OpenSim software Apache-2.0. Models and dependencies require separate checks.

sources.candidateUse: Offline mechanics inspection and reference simulation.

sources.title: OpenSim Moco: Musculoskeletal optimal control
supports: Direct collocation for tracking, prediction, muscle recruitment and parameter estimation.
Examples compare recruitment against EMG and demonstrate solution verification.
limitations: Costs and constraints influence estimated recruitment; EMG timing agreement is not force identification.
Forward replay can need stabilizing feedback; an optimized trajectory is not an adaptive online controller.

license.value: Article CC BY; Moco code Apache-2.0; CasADi dependency LGPL. Distribution terms need version-specific review.

sources.candidateUse: Generate bounded offline reference trajectories and quantify objective sensitivity.

sources.title: What's New in OpenSim 4.6
supports: Documents SynergyController and Moco compatibility, plus contemporary examples and packages.
limitations: Linear synergy controls do not establish biological circuit fidelity.
Release documentation is not evidence that this workspace installs or reproduces OpenSim 4.6.

license.value: Core software Apache-2.0; documentation, example and model reuse terms require separate inspection.

sources.candidateUse: Assess offline controller interfaces before pinning a reference environment.

sources.title: MuJoCo modeling: muscles
supports: Muscle activation and force-length-velocity actuation.
limitations: Built-in muscle assumptions require model-specific equivalence checks.

license.value: Engine Apache-2.0; assets separate.

sources.candidateUse: Retain current runtime; benchmark selected mechanics.

sources.title: MyoSuite models and task suite
sources.type: official task and model documentation; rendered label 2.11
supports: Muscle-driven control tasks and fatigue, sarcopenia and tendon-transfer variants.
limitations: Documentation explicitly calls its simplified elbow troubleshooting model physiologically inaccurate.
Arm counts vary across documentation sections; inspect exact XML, asset terms and pinned revision before use.

license.value: Repository Apache-2.0; individual model, mesh and training asset rights require inspection.

sources.candidateUse: Engineering control sandbox; reject simplified elbow as a physiological reference.

sources.title: SCONE core repository
sources.type: official source repository and README; unpinned main
supports: Predictive motion simulation and controller optimization infrastructure.
limitations: Core, Studio and optional simulation engines have distinct licensing and integration requirements.
Repository reading does not establish reproducible performance in the browser runtime.

license.value: Core Apache-2.0; Studio GPL-3.0-or-later; optional engine terms separate.

sources.candidateUse: Optional offline comparison of interpretable controller families.

sources.title: SCONE MuscleReflex and ReflexController documentation
supports: Configurable delayed feedback using muscle length, velocity, force and spindle-like signals.
Source/target muscles and feedback gains can be specified.
limitations: Signals and delays are abstractions; no automatic nerve-root or lesion mapping.
A tuned reflex controller needs separate robustness and intended-task validation.

license.value: Documentation CC BY-NC-SA 4.0; core implementation Apache-2.0.

sources.candidateUse: Reference for explicit sensory delay and reflex-channel design.

sources.title: CEINMS introduction and repository
sources.type: official methods documentation and source repository
supports: EMG-driven, EMG-assisted and optimization-based modes with subject calibration.
Activation/contraction models include rigid and elastic tendon options.
limitations: Torque-matching optimization described as closed loop is distinct from real-time sensory motor control.
Muscle forces remain model estimates; preprocessing, calibration and matching OpenSim build versions matter.

license.value: Code Apache-2.0; experimental inputs and anatomical assets retain separate terms.

sources.candidateUse: Later offline EMG calibration comparison, after selecting licensed synchronized data.

sources.title: Benchmarking of dynamic simulation predictions in two software platforms using an upper limb musculoskeletal model
sources.type: primary upper-limb model and benchmarking paper; 2015
supports: Dynamic upper-limb mechanics benchmarked in historical OpenSim and SIMM implementations.
Passive and controlled tests expose effects of muscle paths and muscle-model differences.
limitations: Generic model and restricted experimental sample/task do not validate all upper-limb movement or pathology.
Linked SimTK download was inaccessible; exact files, modern compatibility and model license are unverified.

license.value: Model redistribution license not verified; publication access does not grant model rights.

sources.candidateUse: Preferred candidate for a scoped mechanical reference, subject to asset and license inspection.

sources.title: OpenSim Upper Extremity Model documentation
sources.type: official model documentation; Holzbaur model family
supports: Describes upper-extremity kinematic and muscle geometry with experimental moment-arm and moment-capacity comparisons.
limitations: This historical kinematic model is distinct from a verified dynamic implementation.
Documentation alone does not establish inertias, asset availability, full-body compatibility or innervation.

license.value: Model license and downloadable artifact not verified.

sources.candidateUse: Compare regional geometry and muscle naming after obtaining permitted exact files.

sources.title: A dataset for the investigation of upper limb torque prediction from EMG signals
sources.type: primary dataset landing page; v1 published 2024
supports: Describes 17 participants, elbow and combined shoulder/elbow tasks, raw and processed EMG, kinematics and scaled models.
limitations: Archive not downloaded; license was not displayed in retrieved landing-page text.
Torque files exist, but measured versus inverse-derived provenance remains unresolved because linked methods were inaccessible.

license.value: Dataset permission unverified; do not infer from public download availability.

sources.candidateUse: First-elbow dataset candidate after rights, torque derivation and synchronization checks.

sources.title: A calibrated database of kinematics and EMG of the forearm and hand during activities of daily living
supports: Describes 22 participants, 26 activities, calibrated hand angles and raw/normalized forearm EMG.
limitations: Forearm recording zones are not isolated signals for every anatomical muscle.
Files and license metadata were not verified; not an elbow torque or whole-body dataset.

license.value: Dataset license not visible in retrieved landing-page text.

sources.candidateUse: Later hand/forearm task reference after license and channel inspection.

sources.title: A Kinematic and EMG Dataset for Upper Limb and Hand Movement Analysis in Post-Stroke and Healthy Subjects
sources.type: primary data descriptor; Scientific Data, December 2025
supports: Synchronized surface EMG and marker-derived movement for ten healthy and ten post-stroke participants performing six functional tasks.
Methods describe preprocessing, missing-marker handling and signal quality checks.
limitations: Small, differently aged groups are not population norms or lesion-mechanism ground truth.
Derived angles and gap-filled trajectories are processed observations; archive and code were not downloaded.

license.value: Dataset CC BY 4.0 explicitly stated; article CC BY-NC-ND 4.0; code terms require artifact inspection.

sources.candidateUse: Later observed pathological comparison with held-out participants and missing-data flags.

sources.title: AddBiomechanics downloadable data
sources.type: official dataset and provenance documentation; reviewed core v1.0
supports: Reviewed core combines experimental markers and ground reaction forces with estimated skeletons, kinematics and joint torques.
Documentation distinguishes reviewed core data from broader public uploads.
limitations: Inverse-dynamics torques are estimates; uploaded datasets vary in quality and upper-limb marker coverage.
No archives downloaded; source-study provenance and dataset-specific conditions still require inspection.

license.value: Listed datasets CC BY 4.0, with original-source citations retained; software licensing is separate.

sources.candidateUse: Later locomotion references selected for task, markers, forces and provenance.

sources.title: AddBiomechanics: Automating model scaling, inverse kinematics, and inverse dynamics from human motion data through sequential optimization
supports: Sequential estimation of model scaling, marker registration, kinematics and dynamics.
limitations: Marker-registration ambiguities and anthropometric priors affect identification.
Validation of an automated pipeline is not direct validation of muscle forces or patient-specific pathology.

license.value: Article CC BY; pipeline software and data have separate licenses.

sources.candidateUse: Document estimated-channel provenance and scaling uncertainty.

sources.title: OpenCap: Human movement dynamics from smartphone videos
supports: Video-based pose estimation, marker augmentation and musculoskeletal optimization produce movement and dynamics estimates.
Validation used laboratory measurements from ten healthy participants across selected tasks.
limitations: Healthy-task results do not establish injury-cohort transfer.
Published upper-limb and lumbar actuation uses ideal torque motors, not muscles.
Learned inference and optimization require independent task/domain evaluation.

license.value: Article CC BY; source, weights, validation data and hosted-service permissions need separate checks.

sources.candidateUse: Later capture/reference option; distinguish observed video from estimated biomechanics.

sources.title: OpenCap core repository and license
supports: Core pipeline produces 3D marker trajectories and OpenSim kinematics from videos; dynamics workflow is separate.
limitations: Source license does not establish all model-weight, upstream-data or hosted-service rights.
No checkout, installation, exact commit or reproducibility run completed.

license.value: Core Apache-2.0 verified; other assets and service terms require inspection.

sources.candidateUse: Inspect offline capture pipeline and artifact terms before integration.

sources.title: Is My Model Good Enough? Best Practices for Verification and Validation of Musculoskeletal Models and Simulations of Movement
supports: Separate numerical verification, intended-use validation and independent data.
limitations: Guidance does not validate this implementation.

license.value: Publication reuse grant unverified.

sources.candidateUse: Frame scoped experiments.

sources.title: Converting biomechanical models from OpenSim to MuJoCo
supports: Demonstrates conversion and parameter fitting for one constrained upper-limb model in OpenSim 4.0 and MuJoCo 2.0.
limitations: Historical versions, approximate paths and a fixed torso limit generalization.
Test trajectories also used optimized corrective controls; this is not zero-shot mechanical equivalence or a universal speed guarantee.

license.value: Paper and conversion-code redistribution terms were not verified.

sources.candidateUse: Design independent conversion checks; do not assume format translation preserves physiology.

sources.title: Cortical Spiking Network Interfaced with Virtual Musculoskeletal Arm and Robotic Arm
supports: A small layered spiking network controls a two-degree-of-freedom virtual arm using muscle-length feedback and reinforcement.
limitations: Virtual control is task-restricted; robotic mirroring is open loop and grasp is scripted.
No whole cortex, comprehensive peripheral physiology or clinical lesion prediction is established.

license.value: Article CC BY; linked model/code artifact license requires inspection.

sources.candidateUse: Future isolated research experiment after mechanics and feedback baselines.

sources.title: Optimal feedback control as a theory of motor coordination
supports: Task goals, feedback, state estimation and noise explain selected coordination and variability patterns.
limitations: Computational-level theory leaves neural implementation and learning mechanisms unresolved.
Simplified task models do not identify nerve-root injury effects.

license.value: Publication copyright stated; permissive redistribution grant not verified.

sources.candidateUse: Motivate functional planner/state-estimator abstractions with explicit task boundaries.

sources.title: Predicting gait adaptations due to ankle plantarflexor muscle weakness and contracture using physics-based musculoskeletal simulations
supports: Planar muscle-driven gait with optimized controllers explores weakness and contracture after healthy-gait comparisons.
limitations: Controller re-optimization per impairment is distinct from immediate online adaptation.
Sagittal constraints exclude several compensations; isolated parameter changes do not reproduce an entire diagnosis.

license.value: Article CC BY; linked project artifacts require separate license inspection.

sources.candidateUse: Later lower-limb hypothesis study with restricted claims.

sources.title: Investigation of neural and biomechanical impairments leading to pathological toe and heel gaits using neuromusculoskeletal modelling
supports: A planar model varies reflex feedback, strength and contracture from an optimized healthy baseline.
limitations: Some hypothesized pathological patterns are only partly reproduced; conclusions depend on controller and mechanical assumptions.
Results do not determine patient-specific neural lesions or full three-dimensional compensations.

license.value: Publication and model reuse terms not verified.

sources.candidateUse: Compare explicit neural and mechanical perturbations as hypotheses.
